correctness.rationale: For C² real φ on a bounded connected domain, failure of plurisubharmonicity gives a point and negative Levi direction. P=vv*+δI is positive definite with tr(HφP)<0 for small δ, and any positive definite Hermitian P is of the form conj(A⁻¹)(A⁻¹)^T; strict negativity is open in center and A. Since Gaussian-rational points/invertible matrices are dense and nonzero holomorphic f has zero set with empty interior, one finds permitted q,A with f(q)≠0 and strict negative transformed trace. Under w=A(z−q), g=(w,M) and both estimate integrals gain the same constant affine Jacobian. The exact analytic special-tuple Skoda lemma, Proposition 3.8 of arXiv:2609.33300, yields tr(i∂∂̄φ̃)(0)≥−n²/M² as ε→∞; ordinary limits still hold along ℓ∈positive integers. Every M∈positive integers is available, so M→∞ forces a contradiction. Pseudoconvex converse follows from classical Skoda division applied to this zero-free restricted family. Independent rational-matrix checks verified Hessian trace identities in n=1..5, and exact beta-integral second moments E|w|²=M²/ℓ for the J-kernel confirmed the concentration scaling in 48 bounded parameter cases. These algebraic checks do not prove Proposition 3.8; its analytic proof was reconstructed at the cited source, including the C², f(q)≠0, and fixed-M hypotheses.
residual_risks: The crucial source proposition is a nontrivial analytic concentration/curvature estimate; arithmetic checks only corroborate its normalization, not substitute a proof.
The necessity implication depends on C² Levi continuity and f being holomorphic and nonzero; it does not establish a lower-regularity or ≤n-generator variant.
The source uses conventional Skoda normalization p=n; altering this exponent or the tuple length invalidates the reduction.

value.rationale: The main prior theorem requires a universal infinite-dimensional family of holomorphic generator tuples and continuous choices of parameters. The stated theorem identifies an explicit enumerable/testable countable determining family while retaining the same positivity characterization on pseudoconvex domains. Such separable determining sets are natural analytic objects and can support enumeration, approximation, or descriptive-set arguments; this is a motivated qualitative hypothesis reduction, not a random finite-parameter specialization. The result is modest and follows by standard density and subsequence arguments once the source special-tuple proof is known, so no claim of a major new Skoda estimate, finite algorithm, or lower-generator result is made.
residual_risks: The countable test criterion is not minimal or finite, and checking countably many inequalities is not an effective decidable algorithm.
Its value is a conceptual determining-class reduction, not a new quantitative estimate.
If an existing general separability theorem explicitly gives this exact property, the independent incremental value would decrease.
